## Found by the crawl

### MAJOR SITE-02: 58 broken links in a closed part of the page: the site links to addresses that answer an error

**Why it matters:** Each is linked only from a part of the page that is closed when it loads (a tab, an answer or a menu that opens on a click, a link shown on hover), on a page that shows a visitor what opens it: a closed part a visitor opens is as much the page as an open one. A visitor who opens it and follows one of these links reaches an error instead of the page promised.

**Likely fix:** Point each link at a page that exists, or bring the page back (or redirect its old address to where it went).

**In this suite:** the link report (LinkReportTest) asks each address again; it fails only on one broken since the crawl.

### MAJOR SITE-07: At least 7 links and buttons on 2 pages have nothing for a screen reader to say

**Why it matters:** A blind visitor hears only "link" or "button", with no idea where it goes or what it does. Accessibility audits flag it under WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), the standard that laws such as the ADA and the European Accessibility Act are commonly measured by; an automated read shows a likely barrier, not a legal finding, so a person confirms each one.

**Likely fix:** Give each one words: visible text, an aria-label, or an alt on the image inside it (an icon link to a cart: aria-label="Cart").

- /quote: `<button id="occupancyAndUsage">`
- /quote: `<button id="acceptedTerms">`
- /contact-us/become-an-agent: `<button id="checkbox-_R_b4pav5ubsnllb_-0">`
- /contact-us/become-an-agent: `<button id="checkbox-_R_b4pav5ubsnllb_-1">`

- /contact-us/become-an-agent: `<button id="radio-_R_mpav5ubsnllb_-1">`

### MAJOR SITE-33: 3 links to other sites lead nowhere: the pages are gone

**Why it matters:** Sites move and close: a visitor who follows one of these links meets an error page, or nothing at all, on someone else's site, reached from this one.

**Likely fix:** Point each link at where the page lives now, or take it out. The suite's link report asks every one again on each run, and fails when one that answered stops.

### MAJOR SITE-20: 1 script, style sheet or data request on 1 page failed to load

**Why it matters:** A script or style sheet that does not load leaves part of the page unstyled or not working: a menu that does not open, a button that does nothing, a list that never fills. Visitors see it; nothing tells the site's owner.

**Likely fix:** Point each at a file that exists (a path changed in a release is the usual cause), or remove the reference.

- /blog/why-frontlines-home-solutions-program-matters-for-homeowners: /_next/static/chunks/098jkrn77vgzt.js (502)

### MINOR SITE-15: 4 pages have no main heading

**Why it matters:** Screen reader users jump to the h1 to learn what a page is, and search engines read it as the page's subject; none, or several competing, says neither.

**Likely fix:** Give each page one h1 naming what it shows; the site's name in the header is not it.

- /: no h1 with words shown
- /quote: no h1 with words shown
- /products: no h1 with words shown
- /agreements: no h1 with words shown

### MINOR SITE-24: 4 security headers no page sends

**Why it matters:** Each header closes off one way the site could be misused (a downgrade to http, a script slipped in, the site framed in another to trick a click). A missing one is a weaker defence, not a sign the site has been attacked; security reviews ask for them, and each costs a line of server configuration.

**Likely fix:** Add the missing headers in the web server or the CDN (one setting each), starting with Strict-Transport-Security.

- /: no page of the site sends Strict-Transport-Security (without it, browsers are not told to keep to https)
- /: no page of the site sends Content-Security-Policy (without it, nothing limits which scripts a page may run)
- /: no page of the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (without it, another site can frame the page to trick a click)
- /: no page of the site sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (without it, a browser may guess a file's type from its content)

### MINOR SITE-41: 1 form field on 9 pages has no visible label, only a placeholder

**Why it matters:** A screen reader reads the placeholder out, so the field is named; but the placeholder vanishes once typing starts, so a visitor who looks back cannot see what the field was for, and placeholder text is often too faint to read. Accessibility audits flag it.

**Likely fix:** Give each field a visible `<label for="its id">`; keep the placeholder, if at all, as an example of what to type.

- /products/virginia: `<input name="zipCode">`, on 9 pages: /products/virginia, /products/maryland, /products/delaware and 6 more

### MINOR SITE-29: The site publishes no security.txt, the file that tells security researchers whom to contact

**Why it matters:** Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.

**Likely fix:** Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.

- /.well-known/security.txt: answered 404
